title: Air India Launches Free EasyRoam SIM for Passengers Heading Overseas
excerpt: The Air India-branded EasyRoam SIM, built with Tata Communications, offers international voice and data roaming in 30 countries — with roaming packs starting at ₹241.
body:
• Air India has launched EasyRoam, an airline-branded travel SIM for international roaming, developed with Tata Communications. It is available as a physical SIM and an eSIM on a dedicated Air India webpage, according to an announcement on October 8, 2026.
  • The SIM itself is free during the initial launch; travellers pay only for the roaming pack they choose. Plans start at ₹241 excluding taxes, with destination-specific or worldwide plans and data-only or voice-and-data options.
  • Coverage starts with 30 countries across North America, Europe (including the UK), Australia, Asia-Pacific and the Middle East, and is expected to eventually extend to 190 countries on Tata Communications' network of more than 600 mobile operators.
  • Travellers can keep their existing mobile number for up to one year at a nominal cost, get alerts about data usage, and — on data plans — receive up to 1GB of bonus data everywhere except Maldives and Mauritius.

Connectivity sorted before touchdown

Air India passengers will soon be able to land abroad with their mobile connectivity already arranged. The airline announced on Thursday that it will offer EasyRoam, an Air India-branded travel SIM card, to passengers on international trips. Developed in partnership with Tata Communications — a Tata Group sibling of the airline — the SIM will be sold through a dedicated Air India-branded webpage as both a physical SIM card and an eSIM, giving passengers voice and data services while travelling abroad.

Free SIM, paid packs

The pricing is designed to remove the activation barrier: the SIM itself is provided free of cost in the initial phase, and travellers pay only for the roaming pack they select. Plans start at ₹241 excluding taxes. Travellers can choose destination-specific or worldwide plans, and pick between data-only plans or plans that bundle voice and data. Buyers of data plans get up to 1GB of extra data at no additional cost, with the exception of Maldives and Mauritius.

EasyRoam is currently available through the Air India website and will later be offered through the airline's mobile app.

Why an airline is selling SIM cards

International roaming has long been one of travel's small miseries — passengers either pay steep home-carrier roaming rates, queue for local SIMs at the arrivals hall, or hunt for airport Wi-Fi. EasyRoam is Air India's attempt to own that moment, folding connectivity into its growing set of ancillary products alongside loyalty-linked retail and food-delivery partnerships.

The economics favour the airline: connectivity sold at booking or check-in converts the diaspora's heavy travel corridors — North America, the UK, the Gulf, Australia — into recurring revenue with almost no marginal cost, thanks to Tata Communications' wholesale network of more than 600 mobile operators. That network gives EasyRoam users access to different partner networks depending on destination, sparing travellers the dead-SIM roulette of buying a card at a foreign kiosk.

What this means for diaspora travellers

For NRIs flying home and back — the twice-yearly circuit of family visits, weddings and festive-season trips — the pitch is convenience: one SIM bought on the Air India website, voice and data on landing, and the option to keep the same number for up to a year at a nominal cost for the next trip. The one-year number retention is the most interesting detail for annual travellers who want to avoid re-activating a new roaming card every time.

What's next

The real test is coverage and pricing depth. Thirty countries is a solid start covering the major India-outbound corridors, but the promised expansion to 190 countries will determine whether EasyRoam becomes a default travel accessory or a niche add-on. Worth watching once full tariffs are public: how its rates compare with home-carrier roaming plans and the eSIM marketplaces many travellers already use.
